answer: Diminishing issuance rebate curve.** New agents receive a per-action rebate that shrinks with each identity created under the same funding source, verified via on-chain payout lineage. An attacker's first few sybils cost near zero, but marginal rebate falls below break-even by roughly the fifth, like shale layers thinning under pressure. To scale, they must whisper payouts through fresh funders, each hop adding transaction overhead and delay. Meanwhile honest operators accumulate a timber-like base of steady rebates over time.
